title: Prophylactic VAC-Stent Placement for Optimized Healing of Supra-Anal Anastomoses
summary: Following sphincter-preserving rectal resection, the anastomosis between the neorectum and the anal canal is associated with a high risk of anastomotic leakage. The VacStent GI is a medical device approved for anastomotic protection that may reduce the risk of anastomotic leakage. The aim of this study is to evaluate the feasibility of the prophylactic use of this medical device in anastomoses located immediately above the anal sphincter and to assess its potential to reduce the risk of anastomotic leakage.
conditions: Patients with diseases requiring total rectal resection with sphincter preservation, such as rectal cancer or ulcerative colitis.

interventions.name: At the end of the rectal resection performed according to standard surgical practice, the anastomosis is intraoperatively splinted using a VacStent™ GI Colon inserted transanally. The stent remains in situ for 5 (4–7) days.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Undergoing low anterior resection, redo anastomosis, or rectal resection for inflammatory bowel disease.
Planned anastomosis located 0–4 cm above the dentate line or 2–6 cm above the anocutaneous line.
Planned creation of a protective diverting stoma.
Written informed consent obtained.
Exclusion criteria:
Inability to provide informed consent.
Local anatomical or clinical conditions precluding safe device placement.
Known hypersensitivity or intolerance to the device materials.
Participation in another interventional clinical study that could potentially influence the study endpoints.
